sources.title: The stylistic origin of Bambata and the spread of mixed farming in southern Africa

sources.originalChronology: The abstract distinguishes pottery dispersal around 200 from mixed-farming communities around 350.
sources.scopedClaim: Huffman's reconstruction of Bambata pottery spreading with hunter-gatherer groups into southeastern Africa; no precise locality, migration date or beginning of farming is established here.

date.noteEn: This approximate date follows Huffman's reconstruction in the public abstract. It concerns pottery dispersal with hunter-gatherers; his later date around 350 for mixed-farming communities is a separate development. The underlying excavation evidence was not reviewed here.

events.titleEn: Bambata pottery spreads into southeastern Africa
events.summaryEn: In Huffman's reconstruction, hunter-gatherer groups carry Bambata pottery into southeastern Africa around 200 CE.
events.selectionNote: A regional transfer of pottery practices, selected for the distinction between dispersal among hunter-gatherers and the later presence of mixed-farming communities. No exact settlement foundation or continent-wide migration is claimed.

review.reviewedBy: Codex independent source and English check

date.noteEn: The year identifies the end of Eastern Han and Cao Pi's seizure of its throne. It does not date all three kingdoms' proclamations or the start of his separate nine-rank recruitment reform. No month or day is established here.

events.titleEn: Cao Pi takes the Eastern Han throne
events.summaryEn: After succeeding Cao Cao, Cao Pi takes the throne from the Eastern Han emperor and establishes Wei's imperial claim.
events.selectionNote: The end of a dynasty and assertion of Wei's imperial authority constitute a major regional political change. The episode is distinct from Cao Cao's relocation of the Han court in 196 and Cao Pi's already cataloged nine-rank recruitment system.

review.reviewedBy: Codex independent source and English check

date.noteEn: The Smithsonian explicitly dates the dynastic overthrow and founding to 224. This entry does not assign a day to the battle or imply that every Parthian territory came under Sasanian control that year.

events.summaryEn: Ardashir defeats the Parthians and establishes Sasanian dynastic rule in Iran.
events.selectionNote: A major change in the ruling dynasty of Iran. This marks the foundation of Sasanian rule, rather than dating the empire's later territorial extent, institutions or wars to its first year.

review.reviewedBy: Codex independent source and English check

date.noteEn: Chen reports Sugimoto's 229 and Watabe's 243–252 datings and proposes 244–247. The numeric bounds preserve these alternatives; they do not describe a 23-year mission. This is the mission to Funan, separate from Funan's embassy to Wu in 243.

events.titleEn: Wu sends Zhu Ying and Kang Tai to Funan
events.summaryEn: The envoys Zhu Ying and Kang Tai travel from Wu to Funan. Historians disagree about the mission's date and the Funan ruler they met.
events.selectionNote: An interregional diplomatic mission between Wu and Funan, retained with all three chronological proposals reported in Chen's abstract. The competing proposals come through one study; the underlying chronicles and other historians' works were not independently examined.
